literal_reason: The localization problem is real (P6 never visits sofa/armchairs/diningtable/ottoman and hits the step limit; P3 never reaches the mug and cycles), and broadening is supported: in P1 the box was found only after reaching coffeetable 1 (P1:36), which is exactly the surface class u1 adds. u1 is therefore kept. u2's problem is executable scope: the Actor can see only the current observation and the last two observation/action pairs, so 'a receptacle you have already confirmed empty' and 'a run of steps that only revisits... as a stuck-search signal' are not determinable global-state triggers. Memory M3 and M6 record that this same anti-cycling wording was added previously and was not reliably followed, with cycling/step-limit failures persisting (P1:15/P1:20/P1:24, P3:28-P3:30, P6:26/P6:38 all re-walk already-seen empty containers). Instead of repeating a non-executable absolute more strongly, I narrow u2 to local, Actor-visible triggers: do not re-examine the currently-open receptacle that visibly lacks the target, avoid destinations named in the current observation or last two pairs, and break an observable A-B-A bounce, keeping the first-pass completion boundary. The narrowed u2 does not conflict with u1 (inspect each candidate on first arrival) and the necessary non-repetition behavior is preserved. The existing Checks still observe u1/u2 behavior and are kept unchanged.
applied_text_for_diagnostic_only:
- After arriving at a receptacle that is already open and visibly lacks the exact target, do not examine or re-open it again; choose a different admissible go-to destination instead.
- When choosing the next destination, avoid any receptacle that appears in your current observation or in the last two observation/action pairs; prefer one you have not just visited, so consecutive moves do not bounce between the same two receptacles.
- Keep breaking an observed A-B-A bounce by moving on to another listed receptacle type or instance; continue until the exact target is located or the remaining untested receptacles you can identify from the current listing have been visited once.
